A worked dimensional-weight example

This is an illustrative calculation, not an OOPBUY route quote. Assume a packed parcel weighs 3.2 kg and measures 40 × 30 × 25 cm. If a hypothetical route uses a divisor of 6,000 cm³/kg and charges the greater of actual and dimensional weight, its dimensional result is 30,000 ÷ 6,000 = 5 kg. The comparison would start from 5 kg before applying that route's billing increments and charges.

InputIllustrative valueWhere to verify it
Actual weight3.2 kgFinal packed-parcel measurement
Outer dimensions40 × 30 × 25 cmFinal outer carton, not product dimensions
Route divisor6,000 cm³/kgSelected route's current billing rules
Dimensional result5 kgLength × width × height ÷ divisor

A different divisor or billing method changes the answer. Enter the real destination and contents, then read the eligible route's rules before calculating. No fixed USD-per-kilogram rate follows from this example. Add the resulting freight estimate to the complete haul cost ledger rather than treating freight as the entire order budget.
